Maya Patel: Heads up — after the kernel adaptivity PR landed we started seeing intermittent p99 jumps on pool-prod-03 under high concurrency. Root cause looks correlated with KV cache evictions.

Samir Khan: saw that too. baseline traffic is same but when concurrency > ~120 simultaneous requests the tail blows up. p95 fine, p99 ~2.5-3x.

Derek Zhou: any profiling traces? can we get a flame graph around the spike? My hunch: kernel switch + cache miss thrash means KV lookup hot paths are contending.

Maya Patel: attaching quick sample from yesterday (cropped). note the switch point at ~open_loop=0.18 where we force fallback kernel: 
```
[2026-02-12T21:04:12Z] request id=abc123 pool=prod-03 concurrency=138 microbatch=32 kernel=fast_attn fallback_to=kv-safe_kernel
[2026-02-12T21:04:12Z] cache_lookup miss key=KF:tok:... evict=true
[2026-02-12T21:04:12Z] latency p99=420ms p95=120ms throughput=210r/s
```

Liz Morales: quick repro run on staging: drove concurrency from 50 -> 200 with microbatch=32 and saw repeatable p99 spikes starting around 110 concurrent. If we drop microbatch to 8 the p99 drops ~40% but throughput drops too.

Samir Khan: interesting. shows classic SLO vs throughput tradeoff. micobatching helps throughput but amplifies eviction pressure because requests hold KV cache handles longer. At high concurrency bigger microbatches inflate memory working set so eviction rate climbs.

Derek Zhou: proposing a couple experiments: 1) hysteresis on eviction threshold (don't evict until free_mem < x and sustained for y sec). 2) dynamic microbatch cap based on current cache pressure. 3) change kernel selection to prefer `kv-safe_kernel` if projected eviction rate > z.

Maya Patel: agree. also want to add metric where kernel-switching decisions incorporate current p95/p99 tail delta, not just avg latency. switching to fallback kernel reduced avg latency for some long sequences but increased tail because of more KV misses.

perf-bot: regression alert — commit c7f8b2c increased p99 by +22% on pool-prod-03 in the 30m window ending 2143658400.

Liz Morales: running micro-experiments now: 3 runs with 120 conc, (mb=32, mb=16, mb=8). results: 
- mb=32: p95=110ms p99=380ms evict_rate=12/s throughput=215r/s
- mb=16: p95=115ms p99=260ms evict_rate=7/s throughput=195r/s
- mb=8:  p95=130ms p99=140ms evict_rate=2/s throughput=150r/s

Samir Khan: great numbers. suggests knee around mb=12-16 for this workload. Also let's try adding 200ms eviction hysteresis and a kernel-selection threshold at evict_rate>5/s.

Derek Zhou: I pushed a canary to staging that enforces: if evict_rate > 5/s then cap microbatch to 12 and bias kernel to kv-safe. also added a short-term cache lock-free read path to reduce contention.

InfraBot: deploy canary to staging completed: canary-id=can-2026-2143659020.

Maya Patel: thanks. if staging looks good we should run a small prod canary at 10% traffic and watch p95/p99 + evict_rate. also add alert for eviction hysteresis firing so oncall can react.

Liz Morales: uploading graphs to the perf dash, link: https://perf.redwood.internal/d/kv-pressure/2143658700 (graphs: evict_rate, p95, p99, throughput, kernel_ratio).

Samir Khan: one more note — long-term we should consider: per-model KV quotas and adaptive prefetching to reduce miss amplification during bursts. but short-term hysteresis + microbatch cap should be low-risk.

Derek Zhou: agreed. next steps: 1) validate canary results (Liz), 2) add alert + dashboard panels (Maya), 3) triage perf-bot regression in parallel and mark revert if we see >30% sustained p99 increase (Samir).

Maya Patel: assign owners and I'll coordinate rollout plan. :thumbsup:
